privileges.name: Formal Guilds
privileges.desc: Federations and associations of merchants have loosely existed throughout our nation's history. However, we could choose to placate the most powerful traders across our markets by formalizing their participation in a centralized and officially recognized corpus. Such a privilege will undoubtedly impact both our foreign and domestic policies.

privileges.name: Trade Monopolies
privileges.desc: Giving the most powerful merchants in our countries exclusive trading rights to our mercantile goods to powerful merchants will greatly increase the influence of our most prominent traders. This policy will influence our national attitude towards foreign merchants.

privileges.name: Control over Monetary Policy
privileges.desc: The finances of our nation are a topic of great importance as we strive to improve and perfect our ledgers. Perhaps it would be a good idea to entrust the wealthy members of our society with such a task, and in return provide them with reduced taxation on their commodities and assets.

privileges.name: Building Rights
privileges.desc: Developing our settlements and cities is a costly endeavor. By granting building rights to the local population, we will ultimately reduce the overall end cost of development. However, giving the people such an allowance will considerably increase their influence.

privileges.name: Royal Burgh Commissioners
privileges.desc: The Royal Burgh Commissioners, representing the Crown-chartered burghs of Scotland, convene regularly to safeguard their privileges, regulate commerce, and advise the nation's ruler. Through their collective authority in the Convention of Royal Burghs, they ensure that Scotland's trading communities remain vital to governance, economy, and law, standing as a counterweight to the power of the Nobility and Clergy.

privileges.name: Guild Investments
privileges.desc: The guilds have agreed to divert a portion of their funds toward making improvements to our production process. Though many of these ventures will likely fail, a few may yield breakthroughs that can reshape our capital economy.

privileges.name: Al-Qā'id
privileges.desc: By appointing a loyal Qā'id to oversee provinces and regulate trade on behalf of the state, we empower urban merchants while ensuring provincial governance. Our central treasury draws a stable customs revenue from the Qā'ids' supervised markets, and our tax-farms become a predictable cornerstone of state finance rather than the unstable patchwork they replaced. This institutional layer of provincial trade-administration gives the Maghrebi treasuries a steady commercial revenue that surrounding states cannot replicate.

privileges.name: Moneylending Toleration
privileges.desc: Despite canonical prohibitions on usury, the Crown formally permits Jewish moneylenders to operate within the realm. Cheaper credit flows to borrowers of all classes — though the Church condemns the practice outright, and nobles who owe debts to Jewish lenders are none too pleased.

privileges.name: Tax Farming Grant

privileges.name: Diaspora Trade Network
privileges.desc: The Crown extends legal recognition and protection to the trans-regional merchant networks of the Jewish communities, integrating their contacts, credit instruments, and market knowledge into the state's commercial infrastructure. Jewish merchants gain official patronage as indispensable agents of long-distance trade, and the burgher class grows in institutional weight as the custodian of this commercial apparatus.

privileges.name: Bet Din Commercial Courts
privileges.desc: Rabbinical courts are granted jurisdiction over commercial disputes, providing a faster and more specialized venue for mercantile litigation than the royal courts. The efficiency of the system improves the state's capacity to collect revenues, and the merchant class gains institutional influence through its mastery of commercial law. Noble lords, accustomed to presiding over local justice, resist the erosion of their judicial authority.

privileges.name: Kahal Self-Governance
privileges.desc: The Crown grants the communal councils — the kehillot — formal authority to administer internal communal affairs, adjudicate minor disputes, and collect communal levies. The arrangement distributes the burden of local governance, reducing the cost of maintaining civil order and pushing the realm toward a more decentralized social compact. Noble governors find their authority increasingly contested by councils that answer to rabbinical tradition rather than feudal hierarchy.

privileges.name: Promote Cultural Unity
privileges.desc: The basis of a strong and coherent society is essentially the promotion of one culture to unite all our people and protect them from foreign influences.

privileges.name: Embellish Great Works of Faith
privileges.desc: There is no better way to display our magnanimity and strength of faith than to erect major works or architectural splendor, dedicated to the purity of divinity.

privileges.name: Papal Emissary
privileges.desc: The legates and other emissaries of the ruler are most welcome in our territory. Moreover, we shall also commit to obeying their judgment, and to never interfere in relations between our local Clergy and the ruler.

privileges.name: Freedom of Interpretation
privileges.desc: The many teachings of our faith are like the cool shade underneath a great tree, where all may rest and be refreshed. Under this protective canopy of wisdom, our people are encouraged to think deeply about matters of faith, and to expand and diversify our tenets. This freedom of interpretation will allow our religion to adapt to diverse communities while yet maintaining its core principles.

privileges.name: Waqf Payments
privileges.desc: To demonstrate our piety and religious dedication, we will grant waqf payments as charitable endowments, which shall be used to fund madrasas, hospitals, and mosques, as well as to aid the less fortunate.

privileges.name: Maintain Clerical Proceedings
privileges.desc: Despite our commitment to republican ideals, we permit the Clergy to retain their traditional privileges and jurisdiction over matters of faith, morality, and church law.

privileges.name: State Official Oaths
privileges.desc: All government officials in our domain must swear allegiance to the one true faith under the blessing of the Clergy before they may take office.

privileges.name: Mandatory Clerical Donations
privileges.desc: Our subjects are required to pay tithes to our religious institutions. These mandatory contributions are a divine responsibility, demonstrating the piety and strength of faith our people hold.

privileges.name: Sponsor Printing of Religious Texts
privileges.desc: Circulating printed religious texts is an excellent way to spread literacy and entrench the teachings of our faith firmly within our people's hearts. These efforts to distribute religious literature will educate our people and remind them of their religious responsibilities.

privileges.name: Liturgical Mural Art
privileges.desc: Our palatial walls will be adorned with captivating religious scenes created by the nation's most gifted artists, as a way to showcase the beauty of our faith and profess our love towards the divine.

privileges.name: Apostolic Tax
privileges.desc: Our servitude to the highest authority of the Catholic faith can never be mere promises. By committing to support the ruler, we are sure to win his favor.

privileges.name: Tax Exemption
privileges.desc: Our faith is served by devout men and woman who dedicate their lives to the care and the spiritual well-being of our people. It is only natural that they are not forced to pay any tithe to the government.

privileges.name: Clergy in Administration
privileges.desc: The servants of the faith already possess many skills we look for in administrators. They are well-educated, experienced scribes who follow a higher calling. In many ways, allying ourselves with them would create an efficient and very strong cadre of administrators.

privileges.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Faith
privileges.desc: The unfortunate reality that our religious leaders have a say over our internal politics is only a side effect of the other corrupt deals they have extorted from us under the threat of excommunication.

But, with the support of the true faith, the Ḏimmī shall swear loyalty to the state without threatening the tenets of Islam.

privileges.desc: Jewish communities are confined by law to designated quarters, restricted in movement, dress, and profession. The Church hails the measure as the restoration of proper Christian order, but the immediate shock of enforced segregation falls heavily on Jewish communities.

privileges.name: Torah as State Law
privileges.desc: The Crown formally elevates Halacha as the supreme law of the realm, subordinating secular custom and royal decree to rabbinical interpretation. The clarity of a divinely-grounded legal code reduces the administrative cost of new policies and steadies the social order, while the clergy gains considerable authority as its indispensable interpreters. The nobility chafes at the loss of political primacy, and foreign rulers regard a state bound by alien religious statute with deepened wariness.

privileges.name: Yeshiva Network
privileges.desc: The Crown endows a network of academies dedicated to the study of Torah, Talmud, and rabbinical literature, placing them under state patronage. The yeshivot produce a class of highly literate scholars whose learning extends to law, medicine, philosophy, and mathematics, advancing the frontiers of knowledge across the realm. The clergy, enriched by institutional prestige and royal backing, grows more assertive in its claims on public life.

privileges.name: Sabbath Economy
privileges.desc: The Crown mandates the public observance of the Sabbath throughout the realm, prohibiting commerce, labor, and official business from sundown on the sixth day to the close of the seventh. The weekly rhythm of rest and communal gathering reinforces Jewish cultural distinctiveness, slowing the erosion of identity that contact with the wider world might otherwise bring. Merchants and moneylenders, who lose a significant portion of their trading week, are decidedly less pleased.

privileges.name: Kohen Restrictions
privileges.desc: The Crown formally enforces the purity laws of the priestly Kohanim, elevating them to ceremonial precedence in religious life and restricting their marriages to those of unimpeachable Jewish descent. The priestly caste becomes a living vehicle of Jewish cultural influence, deepening the realm's religious authority and the reach of its cultural identity. The marriage and alliance restrictions inherent to Kohanic law, however, complicate diplomatic negotiations with foreign courts.

privileges.name: Cossack Private Armies
privileges.desc: The Cossacks are granted the right to maintain their own cavalry detachments, mustered at their own expense and pledged to the realm's defense. Their fierce independence and skill in the saddle make them a formidable irregular force.

privileges.name: Cossack Land Rights
privileges.desc: The Cossacks live in their own communities with their own organization. By guaranteeing the autonomy of their territories, we will ensure that they remain loyal to us.

privileges.name: Sanctioned Atamans
privileges.desc: An ataman is the leader of a Cossack group. By officially sanctioning their leadership, we will tie them to our rule, albeit at the cost of giving them more authority.

privileges.name: Allowed Free Roaming
privileges.desc: Cossacks are traditionally semi-nomadic, not permanently settling in any fixed place for long. Allowing them to retain mobility will go far in preserving their way of life... and in keeping them willing to work for us.

privileges.name: Cossack Government Positions
privileges.desc: The harsh life that the Cossacks lead breeds resilient individuals. Instead of permitting them to freely roam our lands, we could recruit the most talented and hardy among them to the administration.

privileges.name: Cossack Military Service
privileges.desc: The Cossacks live in a highly militarized society. Instead of allowing them to freely roam the countryside, we shall incorporate them into our military system so that we may take advantage of their battle prowess.

privileges.name: Protected Faith of the Cossacks
privileges.desc: The Cossacks are traditionally diverse in their religious beliefs, albeit mostly sharing the same faith. By respecting their personal beliefs, we can avoid breeding religious tensions — not only among themselves, but also between them and us.

privileges.name: Respected Cossack Traditions
privileges.desc: The Cossacks have their own traditions and social organization. We need to respect these foundational aspects of their culture if we wish them to truly feel like equal members of our society.

privileges.name: Rada Autonomy
privileges.desc: The administration of the Cossacks centers around the Rada, meaning assembly or council, where they decide upon all matters both military and civil. By giving these Rada legal autonomy from our own administration, we can delegate the governance of their territories to themselves, at the same time as we ensure their complacency.

privileges.name: Registered Cossacks
privileges.desc: Not only shall the Cossacks serve in our military, but shall also be organized with a specific register and their own specific officer ranks, so that they can most efficiently fight in our wars.

privileges.name: Exploration by the Cossacks
privileges.desc: The Cossacks are used to a roaming life, which has taught them to traverse and thrive in almost every type of terrain. We can use these abilities to send them out on expeditions into the unknown, where they will discover new lands for us to take.

privileges.name: Colonization by the Cossacks
privileges.desc: The freeroaming lifestyle of the Cossacks makes them ideal candidates to send into unclaimed regions and make preparations for establishing permanent settlements.

privileges.name: Treaty of Hadiach
privileges.desc: The Treaty of Hadiach concedes many powers and rights to the Cossacks, the most important concession of which being the inclusion of their nation in the Commonwealth, forming the Polish-Lithuanian-Ruthenian state.

privileges.name: Cossack Identity
privileges.desc: The Cossacks have a distinct and proud identity, with their own traditions and customs. They do not easily abandon them due to outside influences, but stand firm and follow their own way of living.

privileges.name: Guarantee Local Land Rights
privileges.desc: A man's home is his refuge. By guaranteeing property rights to heathen members of our society, we will establish a link of trust between them and our administration.

privileges.name: Lighter Taxation
privileges.desc: The secret to a stable multifaith society is simply fair treatment and warm kindness — and, more concretely, tax breaks. By imposing fewer taxes on heathen subjects under our banner, we will ensure their compliance going forward.

privileges.name: Allow Military Service
privileges.desc: The many heathen believers who peacefully occupy our lands are more than willing to defend their livelihoods and their families, should we permit their recruitment.

privileges.name: Promote Tolerance
privileges.desc: Our people frequently cite a desire to build a more diverse and tolerant society. Acting on their behest and following their example, we will treat non-believers with kindness as we strive to achieve stability and prosperity.

privileges.name: Grant Administrative Posts
privileges.desc: Our borders are home to many who do not follow our state religion. Their local leaders are keen on maintaining their positions and beliefs. To cooperate with them and share in their wisdom is the natural path to a healthy administration.

privileges.name: Preserve Local Traditions
privileges.desc: Our subjects come from many corners of the earth, and as such, have different believe and lifeways. From lowly fieldhands to displaced members of their former noble classes, they can all boast of the storied histories and beautiful traditions of their people. To respect and allow the practice of diverse customs is the mark of a superior, harmonious society.

privileges.name: Legal Autonomy
privileges.desc: There are many good citizens in our territory who do not follow our state religion, yet they have been integrated into our legal system and enjoy the same rights as others. Despite protests against their inclusion, allowing them to participate in our judicial framework as witnesses, guardians, and legal representatives of their communities will only further their support of our authority.

privileges.name: Promote Local Hierarchy
privileges.desc: As we strive to maintain social equilibrium, our advisors have deemed it necessary to coordinate with representatives from the many local communities who do not adhere to our state faith.

privileges.name: Pact of Umar
privileges.desc: This treaty clearly defines the status, rights, and responsibilities of 'protected persons' within our realm, including Christians, Jews, Zoroastrians, and many other recognized faiths.

privileges.name: Maẓālim Courts
privileges.desc: Parallel to the authority and existence of religio-judicial administration and Sharī'ah courts, the Maẓālim operate secularly for the affairs of the unbelievers. This grants our Dhimmi subjects standing before a court where they may appeal against the abuses of officials and the verdicts of the qāḍī. Their sessions can take place at the Palace of Justice (dār al-'adl) or a ceremonial hall within the citadel walls (īwan kabīr).

privileges.name: Offensive Military Doctrine
privileges.desc: Our Nobility lean towards aggressive military tactics, ascribing to the idea that a good offense is the best defense. Their commanders and soldiers are predisposed toward bold, decisive action, seeking the swift destruction of our enemies.

privileges.name: Land Rights
privileges.desc: This represents the privileges our Nobility have over the lands they rule and the people who inhabit them. Among those rights, Nobility can usually tax the Commoners living on their lands, draft them to form levies, or mete out justice on their own. These holdings are usually hereditary.

privileges.name: Auxilium et Consilium
privileges.desc: Nobility receive privileges, but they also have obligations to their Lord. They have to provide troops — auxilium — and maintain fortifications and infrastructures in the lands they rule, but they also have to give counsel — consilium — to their Lord when requested.

privileges.name: Nobility Controlled Serfdom
privileges.desc: Among the rights Nobility have over the Commoners in their lands, they can tax them, levy them, and exert justice upon them as needed. Peasants living under these conditions become serfs and are usually bound to the land they worked.

privileges.name: Fortification Licenses
privileges.desc: One outcome of our feudal system has been the proliferation of castles and forts built by the Nobility as a means of increasing their power and authority. That has had further effects on our society, as the Nobility are able to entrench and fortify themselves within their inherited dominions.

privileges.name: Royal Marriage Rights
privileges.desc: The Nobility of our country are considered to be peers to our rulers. Therefore, they are eligible to marry into the ruling family, subsequently increasing their influence and power at court, as well as in the government.

privileges.name: Banal Lordship
privileges.desc: This type of manorial domination developed under the feudal system and is based on the 'ban', which is the authority of a lord to command his tenants, give them orders, and punish them. This has led to the Nobility having greater power in their domains, since they are the ones who dole out justice within their territories and can also tax the Commoners for most of their economic activities.

privileges.name: Primacy of Nobility
privileges.desc: The Nobility of our country has proven to be key allies, as they support most of our enterprises and are the backbone of our armies. For this reason, they consider themselves our equals, and they have become so crucial to the government that we must consult with them before making important decisions.

privileges.name: Only Nobility as Leaders
privileges.desc: Our Nobility believe that they are the only ones capable of leading our armies and navies, due to the events of the past. However, this rankles members of the other Estates, who think that the Nobility are arrogant fools.

privileges.name: Elaborate Court Life
privileges.desc: We have decided to imbue the courtly life of our country with the most elaborate formality imaginable. As everyone who is anyone is expected to attend our ruler in the capital, this restricts how much plotting the Nobility can do against us, but it does come at a high cost.

privileges.name: Protected Faith of the Elites
privileges.desc: The elites have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.

privileges.name: Elite Council
privileges.desc: At a time where the elites are extremely influential — and can precipitate the rise and fall dynasties — it is fundamentally wise to give them certain key positions in the administrative council.

privileges.name: Manorial Courts
privileges.desc: The right to hold court, despite not actually being rulers, is quite a valuable privilege for the Nobility. By emulating their liege and claiming the power to arbitrate disputes, levy fines and taxes, and enforce their own laws, they can amass great wealth and command higher authority across their domain — for better or for worse…

privileges.name: Increased Civic Engagement
privileges.desc: Encouraging the public to engage with sociopolitical matters is an excellent way to safeguard the health of our nation. If they are more involved with the politics and administration of the country, surely they will work harder to ensure its prosperous future.

privileges.name: Inherited Offices
privileges.desc: While it is true that most other realms with administrations like ours tend to hold elections for government roles, we have come to realize that if we are to secure the loyalty of the elites, we must allow them exclusive access to hereditary offices.

privileges.name: Recognized Communes
privileges.desc: Many of our settlements, both urban and rural, have become increasingly autonomous under their landholding elite. While recognizing these breakaways as legitimate entities may reduce our control over their affairs, it will nevertheless please the Nobility.

privileges.name: Appoint Ecclesiastical Offices
privileges.desc: Nobility and divinity are concepts that have become increasingly interwoven within our pious society. The crown retains the right to appoint high church officials, which ensures that the beneficiaries remain loyal to the state while gaining influence of their own.

privileges.name: Control of the Borderlands
privileges.desc: Protecting the faithful who live far from our capital is an arduous task. By commanding the Nobility in those lands to protect their people, we will shield our people against heathens and heretical foes.

privileges.name: Feudal Mercenary Contracts
privileges.desc: The armies levied by our people often leave a lot to be desired. In order to protect our people and best our rivals, we must rely on foreign mercenaries, whose contracts will be managed by the elite members of our society.

privileges.name: Liberum Veto
privileges.desc: This introduces the requirement for unanimous voting in the Sejm. Any noble could stop any vote or legislation by standing up and shouting Sisto activitatem! ('I stop the activity!') in Latin, or Nie pozwalam! ('I do not allow!') in Polish.

Every two months, a lottery is held to reelect the council members. This constant shuffling ensures that the interests of the Republic prevail over personal ones. The fact all its members come from the guilds, though, makes it so that the same families are always the ones in charge.

privileges.name: The Ryad
privileges.desc: The Ryad is the given name to the contract signed between the Boyars and the state. It protects the interests and powers of the Boyars while also defining the responsibilities and rights of the Prince.

privileges.name: Kaigama
privileges.desc: The Kaigama is the governor of our Southern territories and the chief of the army. With power, vigor, and tremendous influence, Nobility who hold this title have at times even played the role of king-makers, as they may decide who shall rule.

privileges.name: Yerima
privileges.desc: The Yerima is the governor of our Northern territories and in charge of levying able-bodied fighters to form the lower castes of our armed forces. While not enjoying as much influence as the Kaigama, we may yet come to rely on what sway the Yerima does have when recruiting soldiers, since we continue to struggle against exterior and interior foes alike.

privileges.name: Cima Fiefs
privileges.desc: As a reward for their victories on the battlefield, we grant frontier territories to our military commanders. This helps to solidify their loyalty to us, and improves the influence our capital has over our distant borderlands.

privileges.name: Office of the Farima-Soura
privileges.desc: Charged with guarding the northern border, the Farima-Soura monitors traffic across the Saharan border, and oversees the safety and swift passage of all mercantile traffic in and out of our borders.

privileges.name: Krajiška Vlastela
privileges.desc: Our borderlands must be safely guarded at all times. privileges.desc: A foundational document that enshrines the rights and privileges of the Nobility. By virtue of this treaty, they are granted exemption from direct taxation, ensuring that they suffer no financial burdens from the state's demands. Moreover, this privilege limits their obligations to provide troops, safeguarding their liberties while enhancing their influence in the kingdom.

privileges.name: Monetary Fiefs
privileges.desc: Rather than granting permanent hereditary fiefs to Nobility, the crown retains direct ownership of most lands and appoints temporary administrators to manage them. These officials enjoy the revenues and authority of their territories only while holding office; upon their death or dismissal, control reverts to the crown. This prevents powerful hereditary aristocracies from forming and bolsters administrative loyalty.

privileges.name: Scholar Officials
privileges.desc:
Our elite class is composed of wise government officials and politicians who gained their enviable positions by proving their knowledge in the national examinations.
The families of these officials may maintain their privileged status as long as they produce at least one official every three generations.

privileges.desc: The upper classes are vultures, devouring the fruits of hard peasant labor and contributing nothing in return. By seizing the means of production, we will place the future of our nation and its people in our own hands!

privileges.name: Fewer Levies
privileges.desc:
The Commoners are the lifeblood of our state. They nourish our population, craft the materials for our buildings, and produce the goods our Burghers trade in.
Although war is a time of great hardship for our state, we must make the effort to keep our Commoners away from the conflict if we want to avoid famine and economic collapse after the war.

privileges.name: Yeomanry
privileges.desc: Freeholdeers with small land possessions receive elevated rights in return for taking on some responsibilities of petty nobles, including having to fulfill higher expectations regarding the defense of the realm.

privileges.name: Common Militias
privileges.desc: The common people are allowed to keep their weapons, which they then must use when called for levy service.

privileges.name: Protected Faith of the Common People
privileges.desc: The common people have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.

privileges.name: Hunting Permits
privileges.desc: Allows the Commoners to hunt and skin game within the legal and physical boundaries of their lord's or township's domain.

privileges.name: No Labor on Sunday
privileges.desc: It would be wise to follow the teachings of the Christian Church and decree our serfs and peasants may have respite from their work on Sundays, as a sign of piety and compassion.

privileges.name: Communal Lands
privileges.desc: Despite the inherently disadvantaged position of the common people, we must nevertheless dictate that all members of the Commoners have the right to establish common flocks of animals and to raise crops in shared fields.

privileges.name: Partial Yield
privileges.desc: The lands of the wealthy are often tilled by Commoners, slaves, or serfs. Thus, the least we can do is award the common people with access to a portion of that land's yield every year.

privileges.name: Access to Royal & Ecclesiastical Courts
privileges.desc: The legal representation of the less fortunate is a vital aspect of a just and balanced society. Public and religious courts should therefore handle legal disputes between Commoners and the elites as fairly as possible.

privileges.name: Commoners in the Administration
privileges.desc: By involving the most skilled amongst the Commoners in our government, we can improve and expand the reach of our administration into the most remote areas of our territory.

privileges.name: Autonomous Villages
privileges.desc: In the rural settlements of our state, there is a saying: 'The laws of the sovereign end at the village's gate.' The people in our settlements organize themselves independently from the central authority of this country.

privileges.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Common People
privileges.desc: The people no longer respect our authority. Indeed, in many cases, they have threatened to take up arms should they be forced to pay their taxes...
